problems.quote: Mobs without a spawn egg (the ender dragon, the wither, an iron golem) get the name without an icon.
problems.issue: All three examples are wrong for 1.21.1. Items.java registers ENDER_DRAGON_SPAWN_EGG (line 1414), IRON_GOLEM_SPAWN_EGG (line 1435) and WITHER_SPAWN_EGG (line 1519), each as a real SpawnEggItem bound to its EntityType, so SpawnEggItem.byId() finds all three and the panel does show an icon for them. Diffing every registered EntityType against every *_SPAWN_EGG item, the only vanilla Mob types with no spawn egg are GIANT and ILLUSIONER.
problems.correction: Use mobs that genuinely have no egg, e.g. "Mobs without a spawn egg (the giant, the illusioner) get the name without an icon." — or drop the examples and just state the fallback.

problems.quote: Being shaped recipes, the middle row is fixed: a mirrored arrangement does not craft.
problems.issue: Backwards. Vanilla ShapedRecipePattern.matches(CraftingInput) tries the horizontally mirrored layout first and the literal one second (`if (!this.symmetrical && this.matches(input, true)) return true;`, ShapedRecipePattern.java:171-187). Neither pattern here is symmetrical, so GGG/MSH/GGG also crafts the Mob Loader and GGG/DSM/GGG also crafts the Mob Unloader. Being shaped constrains the row/column geometry, not the left-right order.
problems.correction: Say the opposite: shaped recipes are mirror-matched by vanilla, so the middle row also works reversed (minecart–saddle–hopper for the loader, dropper–saddle–minecart for the unloader); only the glass frame and the 3x3 shape are fixed.

problems.quote:
Capture and release never happen in the same scan, so a mob needs at least two of them — ten ticks
at the default interval — to travel from the pen into the cart.
problems.issue: The "two scans" part is right (both tickServer implementations `return` after a capture), but two scans are one interval apart, not two. At the default check_interval_ticks = 5 the capture scan and the release scan are 5 ticks apart, so the pen-to-cart transfer takes 5 ticks, not 10. Ten ticks is only the worst case if you also count waiting for the first scan after the mob walks in.
problems.correction: "...so a mob needs at least two of them — five ticks between capture and release at the default interval, up to ten from the moment the mob walks into the pen."

problems.quote: every mob whose hitbox overlaps it counts, nearest to the box centre wins
problems.issue: The tie-break is measured from the centre of the input block, not the centre of the 1x2x1 box. findPenMob builds `new AABB(penPos).expandTowards(0, 1, 0)` (centre at y+1.0) but then calls `nearest(mobs, penPos)`, and nearest() uses `around.getX()+0.5, around.getY()+0.5, around.getZ()+0.5` — y+0.5. A mob standing on the upper half therefore loses to one at foot level even if it is closer to the box centre.
problems.correction: "...nearest to the centre of the input block wins" (the search box reaches one block higher, but the distance is measured from the input block's own centre).

problems.quote: The `create:tracks` tag does not exist, so the track test is always false and the track lookup returns before any Create type is resolved.
problems.issue: The tag does exist without Create: this mod itself ships src/main/resources/data/create/tags/block/tracks.json (replace:false, one entry vanillaplusadditions:chunk_loader_track with required:false). What actually makes isTrack() false is that the entry is optional and train_chunk_loading's shouldInitialize() gates on ModList.isLoaded("create"), so chunk_loader_track is never registered and the tag resolves empty. The conclusion is right, the stated reason is not.
problems.correction: "...the `create:tracks` tag resolves empty (our own optional entry for `chunk_loader_track` is skipped, because `train_chunk_loading` does not initialise without Create), so the track test is always false..."

problems.quote: Release puts the mob at the centre of the output block.
problems.issue: Only true for the unloader and for the break-drop, both of which go through releaseStoredNear(level, pos) with pos+0.5. The loader does not: MobLoaderBlockEntity releases at `cart.getX(), cart.getY(), cart.getZ()` for a minecart and at `seat.worldPos()` for a train seat. The sentence sits in a section that covers both blocks.
problems.correction: "Release puts the mob where the target is: the cart's or the seat's own position for the loader, the centre of the output block for the unloader and for the break-drop."

problems.quote:
The class javadocs on `MobLoaderBlock` and on `MobCartLoaderModule` still
describe the pre-`v1.0.0-beta.54` design
problems.issue: The list is incomplete, and the page presents it as the full set. MobCartBER's class javadoc is stale in the same two ways ("hovering above the block" — it renders at the block centre via translate(0.5, 0.5, 0.5); "pen candidate for the loader, cart passenger for the unloader" — it renders the stored mob), and MobUnloaderBlock's second sentence ("Shows the cart passenger as the spinning mini-mob") is stale too, even though its first sentence happens to be correct.
problems.correction: Add MobCartBER, and note that MobUnloaderBlock's javadoc is only half right — its facing sentence holds, its display sentence does not.
